Hi everyone,

The recent nixpkgs PR to bump lean packages from 4.29.0 to 4.29.1 has gotten a bit out of hand, and due to the author's lack of presence lately, I have begun updating the packages to 4.30.0 instead.

The main problem I faced was that a naïve bump to 4.30.0 resulted in a build failure at stage0:

ln -f ../../../build/stage0/lib/lean/libLake.a ../../../build/stage0/lib/lean/libLake.a.export

The error is similar to https://github.com/NixOS/nixpkgs/issues/423461 but even having set libuv to 1.48.0 as done in flake.nix, the build fails. The workaround was to use Clang 19 instead of GCC (which is the standard in nixpkgs) that used to work with 4.29.0.

What's strange is that this error doesn't turn up when building lean manually via nix develop with GCC (clang removed from flake.nix) and libuv 1.52.1 (so I deduce that the libuv version is not the issue). In a successful build via nix develop the logs from the same stage of the build are:

There's also this error that occurs when using GCC: gcc: error: unrecognized command-line option '--print-target-triple'. I don't think it is fatal as it's only used for the target triple. It is easy enough to hard code in postPatch if we need to.

I wonder what changed in the build infra between 4.29.0 and 4.30.0 that resulted in the mysterious Error 2. What's the current attitude toward supporting both Clang and GCC?

If there are any lean+nix users here, any help would be appreciated. Even an indication of curiosity would provide a boost of confidence. I'll post a follow-up message e.g. when I open a PR to nixpkgs. I'm also curious who is using the nix develop workflow in the lean4 repository since it appears to function well.

For reference, here is the lean 4 source in nixpkgs which I've been trying to update.

P.S. I'm not sure if this should be in #general or #lean4
I don't know how much this helps, but I've been building https://github.com/wvhulle/pretty-lean using Nix for several months now and have never ran into any compilation errors.
I have opened a PR to nixpkgs. I'm working on a writeup of the steps I took along the way and will post a link here once I'm ready (have built mathlib etc.)
